clue.text: Highly unusual station sign

definitions.meaning: very strange or eccentric, slang for something far from the norm
the notice pointing passengers to the exit of a railway station

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same phrase: slang for bizarre, and the exit notice seen at every British station.

clue.text: Announce holiday cottage available in Andorra for one

parts.note: to announce is to state
a holiday let is a cottage rented out to visitors

explanation.surface: An advert for a holiday cottage you can rent in Andorra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available in' only links the pieces to the definition; 'for one' marks Andorra as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny independent country, an example of a very small state.

clue.text: Served on board, sounding vulgar

indicators.note: sounding tells us to take the word as it is heard, not as it is spelt

parts.note: vulgar means crude

explanation.surface: A sailor whose service on board came with coarse language.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a ship's company who served on board are said to have manned or staffed it, a past-tense verb.

clue.text: PC helps re-organise difficult journey

indicators.note: to re-organise the letters of the words before it is to put them in a new order

explanation.surface: A computer that helps you replan an awkward trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yiddish-derived word for a tedious, arduous trek or trip, used in British and American English.

clue.text: Too sensible at first to enter a lift shaft

indicators.note: to enter means the letter goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: the vertical shaft a lift runs in is called a lift well

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of sensible

explanation.surface: A sensible person stepping into a lift shaft, which seems a contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean also or in addition, so the phrase swaps for the adverb in a sentence.

clue.text: An opportunity to learn of this, naturally

definitions.meaning: a series of lessons or classes you can enrol on
put the word 'of' before this answer and the phrase means naturally or certainly

explanation.walkthrough: This entry is the puzzle's theme: every clue with '6' as its definition is a British racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme of study is one sense; the idiom 'of ...' meaning obviously is the other.

clue.text: 6 pet, a strain to listen to

indicators.note: to listen to says the pieces are heard rather than read

parts.note: a pet is a cat and a rick is a strain or sprain, so this says cat a rick

explanation.surface: A pet whose voice is a strain on the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6 down. Spoken quickly, 'cat a rick' sounds like the Yorkshire racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Catterick Bridge in North Yorkshire is a racecourse, an example of the 6-down theme word.

clue.text: 6, a small humble dwelling

parts.note: a cot is an old word for a small cottage

explanation.surface: A small modest home on a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot in Berkshire is a famous racecourse, home of Royal Ascot, an example of the theme word.

clue.text: 6 breaks the law, not a person around

indicators.note: around says the word for a person goes round the other letters

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul'

indicators.note: breaks says the letters of the law are broken up and reordered
not tells us to leave out the a from the letters of the law

explanation.surface: A racecourse that breaks the law with nobody about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' and 'not a' take A from THELAW and reorder the rest as THWEL, which goes inside SOUL by 'around'. '6' stands for 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Southwell in Nottinghamshire has a racecourse, an example of the theme word.

clue.text: Sort of sexual underground?

definitions.meaning: the first half of the word for a fashion-conscious urban man
an underground railway, as in Paris

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about a hidden kind of sexuality.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix completes 'metrosexual', and Paris's underground railway has this name.

clue.text: Beast, decrepit one, losing tail

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a crock is a worn-out person or old car

explanation.surface: An old animal past its best losing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A short informal word for a crocodile, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Almost nicked, I had to be emotionless

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: nicked is British slang for stole
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A thief who almost got caught had to keep a straight face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' looks like 'arrested' but means stole.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive, showing little feeling: an unemotional person is described with this adjective.

clue.text: English used in a few lines and a few more for comparison

parts.note: a para, a paragraph, is a few lines of text

indicators.note: used in means the letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a few more lines, written as three L's, L being the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Instructions for writing a passage of English with a few more lines for comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: drawing a likeness between two things, as in 'draw an analogy'.

clue.text: See 15
6 pounds would get wasted

indicators.note: to get wasted is to be wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Money gambled at the races that will just be wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludlow in Shropshire has a racecourse, an example of the theme word.

clue.text: Temperature in Holy Land mountain: 6

indicators.note: in places the letter for temperature inside the mountain

parts.note: Mount Carmel is a mountain in Israel

explanation.surface: A hot spot on a biblical mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartmel in Cumbria has a small racecourse, an example of the theme word.

clue.text: See 17
6 is back, touring Washington

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for back surrounds the other piece

parts.note: the rear is the back
DC, District of Columbia, is the US capital Washington

explanation.surface: A racecourse returning after a tour of America's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' looks like a reversal signal; 'is' is a link and 'back' gives REAR. '6' stands for 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcar on the North Yorkshire coast has a racecourse, an example of the theme word.

clue.text: Advantage in battle, if on top of hill

definitions.meaning: a slight lead over a rival, as in having the upper hand

definitions.text: in battle, if on top of hill
definitions.meaning: placed before hill, it names Edgehill, the first battle of the English Civil War

explanation.surface: Holding high ground gives the upper hand in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works by completing a name: this word on top of HILL spells a 1642 battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitive lead or superiority over others, as in 'a slight lead'.

clue.text: Firmly fixed wicket into cement base

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a screed is a levelling layer of cement on a floor
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket stump set firmly into a concrete base.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastened tightly with threaded fixings, hence fixed securely in place.

clue.text: Bad year in which to lose an agent

indicators.note: in which says the second piece goes inside the first
bad tells us the letters of year are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: to miss is to lose, as with a chance

explanation.surface: A dreadful year in which a spy agency loses one of its people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' gives EARY, and 'in which' sets the word for lose inside it, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission to represent someone, a kind of representative.

clue.text: Provided for fencing not at first joined together

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords
to wed is to join together in marriage

explanation.surface: Two fencers joined together in partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like enclosing, but it means the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Given money or assets, as an institution supplied with a fund is said to be provided for.

clue.text: Equipment for police officer, finally and disastrously, closes endless dispute

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of officer
closes means the shuffled letters close around the other piece
disastrously says the letters of and are thrown into disorder
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to argue is to dispute

explanation.surface: A police officer finally and disastrously ends a long quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrously' gives ADN, which 'closes' around the shortened dispute. 'Equipment for police' is the definition, so 'officer' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A handheld device that traffic officers use to measure the speed of passing vehicles.

clue.text: Place to hack into a favourite piece of software

indicators.note: to hack into is to break inside, so the abbreviation goes in

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street addresses

explanation.surface: Somewhere to break into a favourite program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' suggests computing, but here it only signals one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A small application, often run inside a browser, is a bit of a computer program.

clue.text: Fails to mature topside of beef — roast ruined

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
topside of picks the first letter of beef, with a nod to a beef cut

explanation.surface: A Sunday joint of topside ruined in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Topside is a cut of beef, but here it picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or pregnancy that ends prematurely without developing is said to come to nothing.

clue.text: 6, strong desire to change the ending

indicators.note: to change the ending means the final letter is swapped for another

parts.note: thirst is a strong desire, as in a thirst for knowledge

explanation.surface: A craving to rewrite how a story ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces T; the theme and the crossings give K. '6' stands for 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsk in North Yorkshire has a racecourse, an example of the theme word.

clue.text: Book about killer not yet ready

indicators.note: about means the book surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book
CO, carbon monoxide, is a deadly gas

explanation.surface: A crime novel about a murderer that is still unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killer' suggests a person, but it is the poisonous gas by its chemical formula.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something in the future that has not yet arrived, as in 'the best is yet ...'.

clue.text: Pin prick finally punctures needlewoman

indicators.note: punctures means piercing into, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a sewer is someone who sews

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of prick

explanation.surface: A seamstress getting a pinprick in her finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needlewoman' reads as one who sews, not a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A long skewer-like spike used to hold meat; a pin in the broad sense of a pointed rod.

clue.text: Record a certain amount but not all 6

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: but not all says the final letter is left off

parts.note: some is an unspecified quantity

explanation.surface: Recording a measure of something, but not the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is a racecourse, home of the Derby, an example of the theme word.

clue.text: 6 sounds browner

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard, not read

parts.note: a toaster browns bread, so it is something that makes things browner

explanation.surface: A racecourse that makes a sound like browning bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The Northamptonshire town is said 'toaster'. '6' stands for 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Towcester in Northamptonshire has a racecourse, an example of the theme word.

clue.text: Cheeky husband in 8s 6

definitions.note: 8s read as 'A Scots', so this means a Scottish racecourse

parts.note: pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: A cheeky husband at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 across plus S reads 'A Scots' 6: a Scottish racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Perth Racecourse in Scotland is the most northerly in Britain, a Scottish example of the theme.

clue.text: Amphibian all but stressed within 6

indicators.note: within puts the trimmed word inside the amphibian

parts.note: a newt is an amphibian

indicators.note: all but means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a marked syllable is stressed

explanation.surface: A small creature placed among the stressed horses on a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket in Suffolk is the headquarters of British flat racing, an example of the theme word.
